news.title: Spain coach De la Fuente says Argentina’s conduct after World Cup final was ‘unacceptable’
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — As FIFA investigates Argentina’s conduct after the World Cup final, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente has described the incidents as “intolerable and unacceptable.” FIFA asked one of its disciplinary prosecutors Monday to report back on testy on-field confrontations after Spain’s 1-0 win in extra time Sunday to dethrone the defending champion. Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes physically tangled with Spain players Eric Garcia and Gavi, and Spain captain Rodri was hit in the stomach as he ran past Argentina defender Nahuel Molina.

news.title: Feeling lost without the World Cup? Six ways to survive the weekend
news.lede: What to watch on TV plus other ways to occupy your time now that the party is over. The 2026 World Cup is over, and the millions of people who enjoyed it now find themselves presented with a yawning chasm this weekend. In the UK alone, ITV and the BBC broadcast approximately 275 hours of live coverage over the duration of the tournament, and something that colossal will be hard to replace. Just because the football is over, we are still brimming with things similarly designed to take our minds off the screaming hellpit that is the world around us.

news.title: Inside Nike’s ‘Rip the Script’ World Cup campaign
news.lede: The World Cup wrapped last Sunday, with Spain beating Argentina in a nailbiter of a final that scored 62.8 million viewers in the US. For some soccer fans, the final whistle marked the end of a whirlwind few weeks. For Nike, the tournament was just the beginning. “The actual, most exciting challenge starts today,” Camilo Andrade, global VP and GM football/soccer at Nike, told Marketing Brew the week after the tournament.

news.title: Friday Discussion: Should college football be played on natural grass?
news.lede: The FIFA World Cup wrapped up last weekend with Spain taking the crown on natural grass at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Per FIFA regulations, World Cup games are required to be played on natural surfaces, meaning that several of the large American stadiums had to lay down sod to meet those requirements. This sparked a debate on the internet as current NFL players decried the fact that they have to play on artificial turf while the stadiums they play at are capable of having natural grass. news.title: How Morocco Turned Football Into a Tool of Statecraft
news.lede: The kingdom is cohosting the 2030 tournament alongside Spain and Portugal, but FIFA has yet to decide where the final will be played. Spain insists the showpiece belongs on Spanish soil. Morocco, however, is betting that a new 115,000-seat stadium outside Casablanca can convince FIFA otherwise. That Morocco is even competing to host football’s biggest match reflects how deeply the sport has become woven into the kingdom and has rapidly accelerated its investment in the sport.

news.title: Argentina players ripped apart over World Cup chaos as FIFA set to take action
news.lede: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente has slammed the behaviour of Argentina’s players following their World Cup final victory. Spain needed extra time to claim a 1-0 win over Argentina at MetLife Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring the winning goal in New Jersey. However, after the final whistle, there were chaotic scenes as Leandro Paredes was sent off for kicking Spain defender Eric Garcia to the floor before grabbing the Barcelona centre-back around the neck. It was subsequently reported by the BBC that the red card to Paredes has been removed, and there will be no disciplinary action from FIFA.
